newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices sink to six-month low then bounce.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices sink to six-month low then bounce.

text.p: World oil prices, extending a sell-off of nearly 15 percent in the last month, fell to their lowest levels since last August as warm weather on both sides of the Atlantic highlighted a growing supply picture.

But prices quickly recovered and the activity was a bit distorted because many traders were attending an industry function in London and others were returning to the U.S. market after the three-day President's Day weekend.
Others felt the recent sell-off was near an end.
World benchmark Brent Blend crude oil for April delivery closed five cents higher at $20.39 a barrel after falling earlier to $20.10, the lowest level for the spot contract since August 28.
The International Petroleum Exchange closed early due to the Institute of Petroleum events here.
In New York, at 1810 GMT, the March crude contract on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) was trading one cent lower at $22.40 a barrel.
It earlier fell to $21.89 to match the small losses in London on Monday when the NYMEX was closed.
"The market went out well-offered last night and I think we're getting follow through from that," said Tony Machacek, an oil broker at Credit Lyonnais Rouse.
Traders were also waiting for the weekly U.S. inventory data, which were delayed one day by the holiday.
The American Petroleum Institute report will be released on Wednesday afternoon and the U.S. Energy Information Administration data on Thursday morning.
"The fact that it is so oversold tells me that you don't want to sell down here," cautioned Tom Bentz, a vice president at ING in New York.

Demand for heating oil, which was a prop for higher prices earlier this year, has dropped off significantly in the last few weeks while supplies were replenished and the weather returned to more moderate conditions.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp predicted well above normal temperatures in the Northeast U.S., the world's largest heating oil market, through Thursday.
Northwest Europe was also experiencing moderate weather.
Futures contracts on gas oil, or heating oil, have tumbled in the last few weeks and dropped on Tuesday to their lowest level since July.
March gas oil closed $2.50 a tonne at $175 a tonne.
At the same time, inventories of gasoline, which will help drive prices heading into the spring season, were starting to swell and some analysts predicted rather sluggish growth in demand.

"The underlying message is clear -- while the industry did experience good demand growth of 2.7 percent in 1996, the major reason for the growth was the demand for heating oil, driven by the cold winter of 1995/1996," analysts at Salomon Brothers said in a report.
"The more important growth indicator of gasoline was indeed quite weak," Salomon said. "We expect continuous pressure on prices in spite of the already steep decline."
It forecast an average 1997 price of $18-$19 for U.S. crude oil.

The end of a strike by public sector workers in oil-producing Colombia also knocked off another market crutch. Labour leaders and government ministers reached a deal to end the strike early on Tuesday.

Hernando Hernandez, head of the main oil workers union USO, said the deal for public sector workers opened the way for the resumption of talks with state oil company Ecopetrol over a new collective contract.
He did not rule out a fresh strike by oil workers, however, if their list of more than 50 demands was not met.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8185
